waves.name: Nightly batch cycle
waves.rationale: All three JCL jobs run only IEFBR14 with no DD statements, and no dataset links them to anything else, so the seed family batch-utility holds and one wave is a sound cut. It carries the whole must-not-break nightly cycle: the wrapper submits JOBA and then JOBB. The wave passes the four tests. The wrapper can be swapped while the old one stays as the fallback. Rollback is reverting that swap. The boundary is job order and return codes. A stakeholder can name it as the nightly cycle on the new platform. The weak test is the boundary, because the tree shows no output to compare. JOBC is carried here only because the extractor counts every unscheduled job as an entry point. The wrapper comment calls it retired, so no port work is planned for it until the client confirms.
waves.unblocks: Nothing else in this tree depends on it: no data, contract or call edge reaches these jobs from another unit. In sequencing terms it is a chore, and no later wave exists to unblock. Its value is retiring the shell wrapper and leaving an order and return code harness for whatever the client adds to the tree later.
